patch_description: Currently the SLSQP polish runs two sequential passes but both restart from the best-so-far point (`best_z`) which is the raw initial layout or a slightly-improved raw result — not from the *repaired* feasible endpoint. The recommendation is to restart SLSQP from the repaired (feasible) point after each pass with tighter tolerance, letting the optimizer make fine tangency adjustments (circles sliding into full contact) from a feasible near-optimal configuration. This is the most direct route toward closing the gap to 2.635. I extend the maxiter schedule to include a longer, tighter final pass (maxiter=500, ftol=1e-14) and always feed the repaired point back in as the next starting point, keeping the best result.
